questions.question: A trader marks his goods at 45% above the cost price. He offers a discount of 21% to his customers. What is his percentage profit (rounded off to the nearest integer)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Markup% = 45%

Discount% = 21%

**Formula used:**

Discount%= (MP - SP)/MP × 100

Selling Price (SP) = Marked price (1 - Discount%/100)

Profit% = (SP - CP)/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price be Rs. x

⇒ Marked price = x + (45/100) × x = 1.45x

⇒ SP = 1.45 × (1 - 21/100)

⇒ SP = 1.45 × (0.79) = 1.1455

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 7?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Divisibility of 7

**Concept used **

The divisibility rule of 7 states that

Pick the last digit of a number, multiply it by 2, 

Subtract the product from the rest of the number to its left. If the difference is 0 or a multiple of 7, then the given number is divisible by 7 

**Calculations:**

According to the concept,

We will check if the numbers are divisible by 7

⇒ 3739 = 373 - 9 × 2 = 373 - 18 = 355 [not a multiple of 7]

⇒ 3661 = 366 - 1 × 2 = 364 [multiple of 7]

⇒ 3659 = 365 - 9 × 2 = 365 - 18 = 347 [not a multiple of 7]

⇒ 3915 = 391 - 5 × 2 = 391 - 10 = 381 [not a multiple of 7]

**∴ The number divisible by 7 is 3661**

questions.question: A new mobile is introduced into the market and is marked at 25% above its original cost price. What discount should be given on the marked price to gain a profit of 20%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked up% (MP) = 25% 

Profit% = 20%.

**Concept:**

SP = [(100 + gain%)/100] × C.P

SP = [MP- (MP × Discount%)]

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the article is 100.

According to the question

The selling price of the article 

⇒ SP = [(100 + 20)/100] × 100 = 120

The Marked price of the article is

⇒ [100 + (100 × 25%)]

⇒ 100 + 25 = 125

Also,

The selling price of the article is

SP = [125 - (125 × x%)]

⇒ x = [(125 - 120)/125] × 100

⇒ x = 5/125 × 100 = 4%

**∴ The discount should be given of 4%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

We know 25% = 1/4 and 20% = 1/5

According to the question, MP is 25% above the CP

So, CP : MP = 4 : 5

Now, the mobile sold at a profit of 20%

So, CP : SP = 5 : 6

Now, CP : SP : MP = 20 : 24 : 25

Here, the discount is (25 - 24)/25 × 100 = 4%

questions.question: Shovik purchases two types of sugar: the first type at Rs. 45 per kg and the second type at Rs. 80 per kg. In what ratio should Shovik blend the first type of sugar with the second type so that, by selling each kg of the blended sugar at Rs. 72 per kg, he makes a profit of 20%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost of first variety = Rs. 45/kg

Cost of the second variety = Rs. 80/kg

The selling price of the mixture= Rs. 72/kg

Profit% = 20%

**Formula used:**

(Quantity of cheaper/Quantity of dearer) = [(Cost price of dearer) - (Mean price)]/[(Mean price) - (Cost price of cheaper)]

**Calculations:**

Let the mean price of the mixture be Rs. x/kg and the ratio of the two varieties be R

72 = (120/100) × x 

⇒ 6x = 360

⇒ x = 360/6 = Rs. 60/kg

Using the concept,

⇒ R = (80 - 60)/(60 - 45)

⇒ R = 20/15

⇒ R = 4/3 = 4 : 3

**∴ The ratio in which the two varieties must be mixed is 4 : 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **

The CP of two types of sugar is Rs.45 & Rs.80

The mixture of these two type of sugar sold at 20% profit

Now, the CP of the mixture will be 72 × 5/6 = Rs.60

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d08c0b9e3c8bd8e09c1249b46885e3305b49b9a08be117a3dd9b24eef54ee4cd.png] 

**∴ The ratio in which the two varieties must be mixed is 4 : 3**

questions.question: If a + b = 12 and ab = 35, find the value of a⁴ + b⁴ – 10³?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find two numbers such that their **sum** is 12 and **product** is 35.

By **inspection**, the factors of 35 are 7 and 5, where 7 + 5 = 12.

Let **a = 7** and **b = 5**.

Required value = 7⁴ + 5⁴ − 10³

⇒ 2401 + 625 − 1000 = 3026 − 1000 = 2026.

**∴ The correct answer is 2026.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a + b = 12

ab = 35

**Formula Used:**

a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab

a⁴ + b⁴ = (a² + b²)² − 2(ab)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ a² + b² = (12)² − 2(35)

⇒ a² + b² = 144 − 70 = 74

⇒ a⁴ + b⁴ = (74)² − 2(35)²

⇒ a⁴ + b⁴ = 5476 − 2(1225)

⇒ a⁴ + b⁴ = 5476 − 2450 = 3026

⇒ Value = (a⁴ + b⁴) − 10³

⇒ Value = 3026 − 1000 = 2026

**∴ The correct answer is 2026.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

The **square** of a binomial is given by (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab.

Higher Powers

To find a⁴ + b⁴, we use the identity (a² + b²)² = a⁴ + b⁴ + 2(ab)².

Sum of Cubes

The **sum of cubes** formula is a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).</p

questions.question: Inside a triangle ABC, a straight line parallel to BC intersects AB and AC at the points P and Q, respectively. If AB = 6PB, then PQ ∶ BC is _________.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

BC intersects AB and AC at the points P and Q, respectively

AB = 6PB

**Concept used:**

By B.P.T = AP/AB = AQ/AC = PQ/BC 

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c7c1174c70c638971ae688993ff7e3bfa67f5b3497c2a0e9d70f44ba54188486.png] 

AB = AP + PB

⇒ AP = AB - PB

⇒ AP = 1 - 1/6

⇒ AP = (6 - 1)/6 = 5/6

According to the question,

By B.P.T.,

AP/AB = AQ/AC = PQ/BC 

⇒ AP/AB = PQ/BC 

⇒ AP/AB = PQ/BC 

⇒ (5/6)/1 = PQ/BC

⇒ PQ/BC = 5/6

⇒ PQ : BC = 5 : 6

**∴ PQ : BC = 5 : 6**

questions.question:
Simplify: 

3p - [3p - overline{p+q} - {3p - (p - overline{q-p})}]
questions.solution:
**Given: **

3p - [3p - overline{p+q} - {3p - (p - overline{q-p})}]

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

As the over bar removes the negative becomes positive and vice-versa but only those signs which are under it. 

3p - [3p - overline{p+q} - {3p - (p - overline{q-p})}]

So the new equation will be

3p - [3p - p - q - {3p - (p - q + p)}]

⇒ 3p - [3p - p - q - {3p - (2p - q)}]

⇒ 3p - [3p - p - q - {3p - 2p + q}]

⇒ 3p - [3p - p - q - {p + q}]

⇒ 3p - [3p - p - q - p - q]

⇒ 3p - [p - 2q]

⇒ 3p - p + 2q 

⇒ 2p + 2q

**∴ The simplified value of given equation is 2p + 2q.**

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 12 days, while A alone can complete the same work in 18 days. How long will B alone take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together can do a piece of work in 12 days

A alone can complete the same work in 18 days

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

One day work of A = 1/18 units

One day Work of A + B = 1/12 units

One day work of B = (One day Work of A + B) - (One day Work of A) 

⇒ B = 1/12 - 1/18

⇒ B = (3 - 2)/ 36

⇒ B = 1/36 = 36 days

**∴ B alone can complete the same work in 36 days.**

questions.question: A man can row 5 km/h in still water. If the speed of the current is 2.5 km/h, it takes 4 hours more in upstream than in the downstream for the same distance. The distance is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed in still water = 5km/h

Speed of upstream = 5km/h - Current speed = 5 - 2.5 = 2.5km/h

Time in upstream = 4 h + Time in Downstream

**Concept used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

Distance for Upstream = Distance for downstream

⇒ 2.5 (4 + T) = 7.5T

⇒ 10 + 2.5T = 7.5T 

⇒ 5T = 10

⇒ T = 10/5 = 2 h

Now substituting the value of T in Downstream then

⇒ D = 7.5 × 2 = 15km

**∴ The distance is 15 km.**

questions.question: A man P purchased a land for ₹4,32,000 on the outskirts of a city. Due to some reason, its value depreciated at 25% per annum and he sold it to Q after 2 years. At this time, the city expanded and new projects of infrastructures started coming up. As a result of the expansion, there was an appreciation of real estate prices at the rate of 50%. What would be the value (in ₹) of the land after 2 years, from the time Q bought the land from P?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P purchased a land for ₹4,32,000 on the outskirts of a city.

Its value depreciated at 25% per annum and he sold it to Q after 2 years.

Appreciation of real estate prices at the rate of 50%

**Concept used:**

Amount = P (1 + R/100)T 

Amount = P (1 - R/100)T 

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

P sold the lamd to Q = 432000(1 - 25%)² 

⇒ SP = 432000 (1 - 0.25)2 

⇒ SP = 432000 (0.75)2 

⇒ SP = 432000 × 0.5625 = 243000

P sold land to Q for Rs. 243000

Now the value of land after 2 years 

Amount = 243000 (1 + 0.5)2 

⇒ A = 243000 (1.5)2 

⇒ A = 243000 × 2.25 = 546750

**∴ The value (in ₹) of the land after 2 years, from the time Q bought the land from P is Rs. 546750.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

The Land's value depreciated at 25%, So after 2 year,

The value from 4² = 16 unit becomes 3³ = 9 unit

So, after two years of depreciation, the value of the land is

⇒ (432000/16) × 9 = 243000

Next two years the land's value appreciation is 50%, after 2 years

The value from 22 = 4 unit becomes 33 = 9 unit

So, after two years of appreciation, the value of the land is,

⇒ 243000/4 × 9 = 546750

**∴ The correct answer is 546750**

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks up his goods by 30% and then gives a discount of 10% on the marked price. Apart from this, he uses a faulty balance which reads 1 kg for 870 g. What is his net profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Multiplier = (**Markup Factor**) × (**Discount Factor**) × (**Weight Factor**)

Net Multiplier = (130 / 100) × (90 / 100) × (1000 / 870)

Net Multiplier = 1.3 × 0.9 × (100 / 87) = 1.17 × (100 / 87) = 117 / 87 = 39 / 29

Profit % = [(39 − 29) / 29] × 100 = (10 / 29) × 100 ≈ 34.48%

**∴ The correct answer is 34.48%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Markup** = 30%, **Discount** = 10%, **Faulty weight** = 870 g instead of 1000 g.

**Formula Used:**

Net Profit % = [(Total SP / Total CP) − 1] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/819023e39fe0f72c1f6f9700fdcca510fa4e9779b78b0e9876db0273bb152c77.png] 

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 g of goods be ₹1.

⇒ **Actual CP** for the shopkeeper (for 870 g) = 870 × 1 = ₹870.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** for 1000 g = 1000 + 30% of 1000 = ₹1300.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** after 10% discount on MP = 1300 − (10 / 100) × 1300.

⇒ **SP** = 1300 − 130 = ₹1170.

⇒ **Net Profit** = SP − CP = 1170 − 870 = ₹300.

⇒ **Net Profit %** = (300 / 870) × 100.

⇒ **Net Profit %** = (30 / 87) × 100 = (10 / 29) × 100 ≈ 34.48%.

**∴ The correct answer is 34.48%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

Profit % due to weight fraud = [True Value − False Value] / False Value × 100. In this case, (1000 − 870) / 870 × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Relationship: SP = CP × (1 + Markup %) × (1 − Discount %). This represents the **price multiplier** effect.

Successive Percentage Change

The effective percentage change for two successive changes x% and y% is [x + y + (xy / 100)]%.
